null_conditions.description: verification_match_rate < 0.80 but failures are attributable to title-normalization ambiguity or network degradation rather than concrete metadata errors, OR resolution_rate < 0.90 preventing a valid census.

contradiction_conditions.description: verification_match_rate < 0.80 with concrete title/year mismatches indicating the METADATA_VERIFIED tier is not warranted for failing entries.

invalid_test_conditions.description: Crossref entirely unreachable, persistent HTTP 429/403 policy block, or script error preventing any valid query => TEST_INVALID_OR_ABORTED; results are NOT fabricated or substituted.

uncertainty_output: Finite census N=117 (no sampling error). Exact counts and rates reported. Title comparison is exact normalized equality; a sensitivity check under loose-containment matching leaves title_match at 117/117. Year comparison is exact integer equality; the 5 mismatches are registry year gaps (4 entries had no recorded year; 1 off-by-one 2020 vs 2019), not title/identity failures.
adjudication_basis: The preregistered external-evidence success criteria are MET on the core claim: verification_match_rate=0.9573 (>=0.95), retraction_signals=0 (<=0). All 117 DOIs resolved via Crossref, all 117 titles matched, 112/117 years matched, zero retractions. The single preregistered sub-condition not met is intra_registry_duplicate_dois_max:0 (observed=1): the DOI 10.1016/s0070-2153(07)81015-5 is listed under two source_ids (GAP002-01, GAP002-08). This is an INTERNAL registry-hygiene redundancy, NOT an external-evidence failure — that DOI still resolves and matches Crossref externally. It therefore does not flip the adjudication to PARTIAL/CONTRADICTED (which are defined by rate<0.95 / rate<0.80, neither of which applies). The 5 year mismatches are minor metadata corrections (backfill missing years; fix one off-by-one), not contradictions. Outcome: SUPPORTED_WITHIN_SCOPE on the external-evidence claim, with two documented minor caveats (year backfill for 5 entries; de-duplicate 1 DOI).
